title: Classifying sets with countable infinite-time decision complexity
formal: Characterize exactly the sets A⊆2^ω having a parameter-free infinite-time decider with a countable uniform time bound, by a necessary-and-sufficient condition on Borel codes expressed through the constructible hierarchy.
definitions:
Use parameter-free infinite-time Turing programs with a read-only binary input tape, a binary work tape and a binary output tape, indexed by the natural numbers, and one common head initially at cell 0. The work and output tapes are initially zero. A finite transition table reads the three current bits, writes the work/output bits, moves left or right (left at 0 stays at 0), and changes state. There are distinguished start, limit and halt states. At a successor stage execute one transition; entering halt ends the run at that stage. At a nonzero limit stage each writable cell takes the limsup of its earlier values, the head resets to 0 and the state becomes limit; the input is unchanged. The first output cell is the answer bit. No real, ordinal or oracle parameter is supplied. Finite integers may be hard-coded in the program. Inputs range over all x∈2^ω of the ambient universe V, not merely constructible reals. Countable means countable in V. A program decides A when it halts on every x with answer 1 exactly on A. The target class D consists of A for which some such program p and some α<ω_1 satisfy t_p(x)≤α for every x. The bound may depend on p, but not on x.

The constructible hierarchy is L_0=∅, L_{α+1}=Def(L_α), and L_λ=⋃_{α<λ}L_α at limits; Def takes all first-order definable subsets with parameters from the given level. A Borel code is a real encoding a countable well-founded rooted tree: leaves are labeled by finite binary words and denote their basic cylinders; internal nodes are labeled either complement (one child) or countable union (children indexed by a subset of N). Evaluation upward defines B_c⊆2^ω. Fix any explicit recursive encoding of these labels and edges. The requested output is an explicit condition Φ(c), stated using levels of L, membership, definability and/or elementary-substructure relations, such that for every A⊆2^ω, A∈D iff there exists a valid code c with B_c=A and Φ(c). Φ may choose particular codes: invariance under every equivalent code is not required. It must have no arbitrary real or set parameter; any named ordinal must itself receive a parameter-free hierarchy definition. This is a classification problem, not a request for an effective procedure that decides whether a code has the property. Equivalently, the function target is χ_D:P(2^ω)→{0,1}. The hierarchy condition supplies g(A)=1 iff some valid c with B_c=A satisfies Φ(c), and g(A)=0 otherwise.
answer_criterion: Provide the condition Φ, all auxiliary hierarchy definitions and complete Lean-checked proofs of both directions of the displayed equivalence. State the ambient set-theoretic assumptions. A reformulation that merely encodes a bounded ITTM computation or repeats existence of a deciding program is not a structural classification. Showing only that members are Borel, or finding only a supremum of their times, is insufficient. This acceptance rule concerns a mathematical characterization and does not claim that syntactic novelty can itself be certified by Lean. In function-target notation prove |g(A)−χ_D(A)|≤1/100 for every A⊆2^ω; since both values are 0 or 1 this is precisely the two-direction equivalence above.
context:
Question 6.1 asks for a hierarchy description of the underlying classes; this card selects the decision class and a Borel-code presentation of the desired answer.

The Borel necessary condition is insufficient even among ITTM-decidable sets, so the code condition must distinguish more than topological complexity.

import_provenance.original_title: Classifying sets with countable infinite-time decision complexity
import_provenance.original_statement: Characterize, in terms of the constructible hierarchy, the sets of reals decidable by an infinite-time Turing machine with a countable uniform bound on its halting times, and the corresponding semidecidable classes. The known suprema of possible times do not characterize which sets have such algorithms.

sentences: Inputs are arbitrary infinite binary sequences.
A single finite program must decide all inputs within one countable ordinal bound.
Every target set has a Borel code.
The task is to distinguish suitable codes by a structural condition in the constructible hierarchy.
This explicitly selected variant treats decision only; semidecision and singleton refinements are separate questions.
